content.user_title: Containerize Apps for Docker and Kubernetes
content.value_statement: Container work often fails because build, runtime, network, and secret handling differ across environments. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable patterns for Dockerfiles, Compose files, Helm charts, and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Generate multi-stage Dockerfile guidance for Python, Node.js, and similar application stacks.
Create Docker Compose service layouts with ports, dependencies, health checks, and runtime environment variables.
Outline Helm chart structure, values files, and release commands for Kubernetes packaging.
Explain common container networking issues, including browser URLs, service names, and health-check hosts.
Recommend production image hardening with Docker Hardened Images, distroless images, SBOMs, and scanning.
Show safe BuildKit secret-mount patterns for private package installs during image builds.
limitations: It provides templates and guidance, not a full project-specific security review.
It does not test generated containers or verify runtime behavior by itself.
Examples must be adapted for each framework, registry, cloud provider, and compliance requirement.
It does not replace Kubernetes operations guidance for live clusters.

use_cases.title: Create a service Dockerfile
use_cases.description: Build a production Dockerfile plan with multi-stage builds, dependency installation, exposed ports, and non-root users.

use_cases.title: Design local service orchestration
use_cases.description: Prepare a Docker Compose layout that connects frontend, API, database, and health checks for local development.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kubernetes packaging
use_cases.description: Convert a containerized application plan into a Helm chart structure with values, services, ingress, and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Containerize this application. First identify the runtime, package manager, build command, start command, ports, and environment variables. Then draft the Dockerfile approach.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker Compose
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose plan for this frontend, API, and database. Include service names, port mappings, health checks, startup order, and runtime environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Package with Helm
prompt_templates.scenario: Move a containerized app toward Kubernetes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Helm chart for this application. Include chart structure, configurable values, deployment resources, services, ingress, config maps, and secrets handling.

prompt_templates.title: Harden for Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this containerization plan for production. Focus on image choice, non-root runtime, secret handling, SBOM generation, vulnerability scanning, and multi-architecture builds.

output_examples.input: A FastAPI service needs a production container plan.
output_examples.output: A multi-stage build plan with dependency installation, a non-root runtime user, a documented service port, and a health-check target.

output_examples.input: A Next.js frontend and API need local orchestration.
output_examples.output: A Compose service map that separates browser-facing URLs from container service URLs and adds startup ordering through health checks.

output_examples.input: A team wants to deploy the containerized app on Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: A Helm packaging outline with values, deployment resources, service configuration, ingress options, and secret-handling notes.

best_practices: Start with an impact analysis of ports, environment variables, network paths, authentication, and build requirements.
Keep real secrets out of images and use BuildKit secret mounts or platform secret stores.
Scan images in CI and prefer minimal, pinned, non-root runtime images for production.
anti_patterns: Do not bake real credentials, tokens, private keys, or local environment files into container images.
Do not use localhost for server-to-server calls inside Compose or Kubernetes networks.
Do not ship compilers, test frameworks, package caches, or build tools in the final runtime image.

faq.question: Can this skill create Dockerfiles for different languages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for Python and Node.js and can adapt the same containerization steps to similar stacks.

faq.question: Does it support Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers services, build arguments, runtime environment variables, health checks, ports, and dependency ordering.

faq.question: Can it help with Helm charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines chart structure, values, templates, services, ingress, config maps, and secret resources.

faq.question: Does it handle production security?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for hardened images, distroless images, SBOMs, Trivy scanning, non-root users, and BuildKit secrets.

faq.question: Will it run or test my containers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces guidance and file patterns. You still need to build, run, scan, and test the containers.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
